rows.text: The extraction chain runs: **concentrate** (gravity, magnets, or froth flotation for sulphides — oil-wetted grains ride air bubbles while wetted gangue sinks), then **calcination** (carbonates → oxide, no air: ZnCO₃ → ZnO + CO₂) or **roasting** (sulphides → oxide, excess air: 2ZnS + 3O₂ → 2ZnO + 2SO₂), then **reduction**: carbon reduction in the smelter where CO made in situ (CO₂ + C → 2CO) strips the oxygen (Fe₂O₃…

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — From Rock to Metal This topic is the engine room of the unit: how a concentrated ore becomes a metal. Four verbs carry it — **calcination** (heat the carbonate), **roasting** (heat the sulphide in air), **smelting with carbon reduction** (coke does the chemistry), and **electrochemical reduction** (electrons do what coke cannot).…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Concentration (dressing) of the ore - **Gravity/washing** — lighter gangue washes away (oxide ores, gold). - **Magnetic separation** — magnetite (Fe₃O₄) pulled from silica by a magnet belt. - **Froth flotation** — for sulphides: powdered ore + water + pine oil + air; sulphide particles are wetted by oil and ride the froth, silicate gangue is wetted by water and sinks.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Calcination = carbonate + no air; roasting = sulphide + air. Thermite = Al + Fe2O3, not an extraction of Al. Hall-Heroult numbers: cryolite, ~950 C, carbon anodes burn. CO in furnace: CO2 + C -> 2CO.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Every step of the chain — float, roast, reduce — exists to deliver one thing to the furnace: a porous oxide. Sulphides and carbonates are merely the oxide's temporary disguises.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Concentration: gravity washing, magnetic separation (Fe3O4), froth flotation (sulphides; pine oil + air, sulphide floats, gangue sinks). Calcination: no/limited air, carbonates/hydrates -> oxide (ZnCO3 -> ZnO + CO2; Al2O3.2H2O -> Al2O3).…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: A single Hall–Héroult pot carries ~200 kA and makes about 1.5 t of aluminium a day; the electricity for one kilogram is roughly 13–15 kWh — the reason smelters sit next to hydroelectric dams.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Describe the electrode reactions and the role of cryolite in the Hall-Heroult cell.  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **Calcination is not "heating in air":** the defining difference from roasting is the **absence of excess air** — calcination decomposes, roasting oxidises.  ·  **Thermite does not extract aluminium:** it *consumes* aluminium to make iron; aluminium itself must be electrolysed first. The exam question "why is Al not extracted by carbon reduction" is answered with temperature + carbide, not with thermite.
